Page 3 · Looking ahead

Next steps and the original reports

When the next exam is due, questions worth asking the doctor, a word list, and the two original PDF reports.

Timeline

Next colonoscopy: about July 2031

Dr. Simien recommended a repeat colonoscopy in 5 years. National guidelines (U.S. Multi-Society Task Force, 2020) suggest 5 to 10 years after one or two small serrated lesions without abnormal cells, so 5 years is on the careful end. That fits a history of polyps.

Between now and then, no special follow-up is needed for the polyps. If new symptoms appear (blood in the stool, a lasting change in bowel habits, unexplained weight loss, or ongoing belly pain), see a doctor sooner rather than waiting for 2031.
For the next visit

Questions worth asking

  1. Is 5 years still the plan now that the lab results are in? The colonoscopy report set the 5-year date before the lab results came back. The results were reassuring, so it's reasonable to confirm.
  2. What were the earlier polyps, and when? The reason for this exam was a "personal history of colonic polyps." Knowing those details helps make sense of the schedule.
  3. Should we add a fiber supplement for the diverticulosis?
  4. Will the billing codes be updated? The report lists code D12.0 ("benign neoplasm of cecum"), but the lab found the cecum polyp was only a tag of normal lining. The report itself says its codes are preliminary. Worth a look if an insurance statement seems off.
Word list

Medical terms in these reports

TermMeaning
PolypA small growth or bump on the inner lining of the colon.
CecumThe pouch at the very start of the colon, low on the right side, where the small intestine joins.
Ascending colonThe section that runs up the right side of the belly from the cecum.
SessileFlat-based, sitting directly on the lining rather than hanging on a stalk.
Cold snareA thin wire loop that cuts the polyp off without heat. Standard for small polyps.
PathologyLab examination of tissue under a microscope.
Mucosal tagA small flap of normal lining. Not a growth.
Sessile serrated lesionA polyp type with a saw-tooth look under the microscope; can slowly become cancer if left in place.
DysplasiaAbnormal-looking cells, an early warning sign. None was found.
Neoplasm / malignancyA new abnormal growth / cancer. The cecum sample was negative for both.
Diverticula, diverticulosisSmall pouches in the colon wall / having those pouches.
DiverticulitisWhen a pouch becomes inflamed or infected. Not present here.
Withdrawal timeTime spent inspecting while pulling the scope out. 6 minutes or more is the quality standard.
